developmental.approach: Conceptual foundations, guided investigations and foundational computing

requirements: Two or three measurable objectives derived from the performance task; MOE mapping recorded as PROPOSED, never claimed
At least two distinct, named misconceptions, each taught against and diagnosed by a block
Hints in every guided scene; no hints or worked steps in independent scenes
Choice items with three or more plausible options, or richer interactions
No system, policy or answer-policy text in learner-visible fields; no generator prefixes; UTF-8 text with no mojibake
Specific learner actions in every scene
Guided practice, independent work, extension and reflection, in that order
An authentic Liberian situation that needs the concept, not a name swap
Formative only: no grade, mastery or assessment keys in the learner projection

objectives.statement: Use geographical vocabulary and a labelled sketch to compare coastal and inland landscapes in Liberia.
Support a comparison with relevant text evidence while distinguishing observations from unsupported generalizations.
Recommend a community reading-club site using local evidence, a counterargument and a question for further checking.

misconceptions.description: Every inland location is assumed to be high or mountainous.
misconceptions.response: Inland means away from the coast. A broad terrain description does not determine every local elevation.

misconceptions.description: One observation or place description is treated as evidence about all communities.
misconceptions.response: Name the place and observation, limit the conclusion to that evidence and seek additional observations.

misconceptions.description: Coastal or inland is treated as enough evidence to select a safe site.
misconceptions.response: Compare the actual site, path and local observations. A region label alone does not establish safety.

misconceptions.description: General coast-to-inland landform descriptions are treated as exact county boundaries.
misconceptions.response: Use an administrative map for county boundaries. A physical sketch does not establish those lines.

misconceptions.description: Evidence about a dry room or a clear path is treated as proving the other requirement too.
misconceptions.response: Check each requirement separately. Room and route observations answer different questions.

answerGuidance.geography: Coastal means near the sea; inland means farther from the coast. The general terrain description is not a precise elevation map or a county boundary. Accept a clearly labelled schematic with no invented distances.
answerGuidance.evidence: The two relevant Club A details concern the dry room and the water-covered path. Location alone does not establish the room or route condition. The records explicitly leave conditions unchecked.
answerGuidance.comparison: Club A: room dry in two showers, part of path covered in one; after-dark path unknown. Club B: roof leaked, path clear in both; river after prolonged rain unknown. Require evidence from both places and one limit. Do not demand one predetermined site choice.
answerGuidance.scope: One room in two showers cannot establish a rule about all coastal buildings or all future storms. Club B's path observations do not settle its leaking roof or its river under unchecked conditions.
answerGuidance.recommendation: Accept either conditional choice or a justified conclusion that neither site is ready. Require consideration of both dry storage and access, an evidence-based response to a counterargument, and a concrete repair or check. No child should be sent to inspect water, roofs or unfamiliar paths.
answerGuidance.transfer: Useful questions ask about actual room leaks, route access, different users and conditions not yet observed. A similar landscape elsewhere does not prove the same local site conditions. Pupils should distinguish questions from invented findings.

segments.activity: Read geography, explain words and sketch sea/coast/inland
Read and select relevant community evidence

teacherGuide.materials: Printed passages, paper and pencil. A pupil may describe a sketch orally or direct a scribe.
teacherGuide.support: Read each record aloud without supplying the comparison. During guided work only, offer room/path headings. Independent responses must retain the same reasoning demand with oral or scribed access.
teacherGuide.extension: Identify a new observation that would change the recommendation and explain why. Compare two different defensible recommendations that use the same evidence.
teacherGuide.factualScope: The order is Regions of Liberia. Stable physical geography is used; no historical narrative, current population, official safety policy or officeholder claim is added. These would require separately verified sources.

sourceChecks.scope: Geography only. No historical dates, population estimates, current officeholders or official policy claims are used.

sourceChecks.fictionalEvidence: All reading-club sites, paths, observations and community decisions in the lesson are explicitly invented teaching cases, not measurements from a real school.
sourceChecks.mapping: Physical regions are generalized terrain descriptions, not county borders. Learner sketches have no scale and cannot locate a real site precisely.

teacherGuide.originalWording: No map, photograph or long text is copied. Geographic statements are short original paraphrases; fictional records are labelled on first presentation. Exact-version rights and academic review remain pending.
teacherGuide.oversight: Read the full comparison and recommendation. Check use of both records, separation of observation/inference, a counterargument and an honest uncertainty. Formative choice success is not independent mastery evidence.
teacherGuide.safety: No outdoor investigation is required. Adults must decide actual venue and route safety; pupil writing is a reasoning exercise, not authorization to use a site.
teacherGuide.offline: Keep geography and both case records available in print. Use a paper sketch or oral description. Do not require an online map, color discrimination, dragging, a field trip or a real location disclosure.
teacherGuide.retention: Propose a different pair of local records after seven days. Ask for a comparison and a limited conclusion. Nothing is scheduled or scored here.
teacherGuide.assessment: All work is formative. No governed test, official grade, promotion decision or canonical mastery update is supplied.
